messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging SRE on-call: Stratus (enterprise VPC) experiencing model degradation in dedicated pool 'stratus-prod-pool'. Symptoms: rising tail latency, sporadic OOMs on workers. Affected tenant: stratus-corp. Severity P2. Link: https://redwood.inc/incident/1812345678

sre_jordan: I’m on it. Can someone drop recent allocator logs and which model variants are active for that tenant?

maya_oncall: grabbing logs now. Noticed a spike in sequence lengths for a subset of requests — policy has been routing to redwood-34b:v3 (quantized) for throughput.

ellen_csm: customer on the phone, they see failed API calls and slow responses for some users. Requesting ETA and whether we can pin them to a safe variant while we investigate.

nira: quick ask — is this hitting only the dedicated pool or also shared-hosted fallback routes?

eng-luca: checking routing table: tenant stratus-corp is pinned to 'stratus-prod-pool' on dedicated. Fallback policy exists but was disabled last week for throughput testing.

ops-bot: recent deploy: 2026-03-15T03:12Z -> worker kernel update applied to stratus-prod-pool. Rollback tag: kupdate-20260315

maya_oncall: logs (excerpt):
```
[03:18:42] worker-12 OOM while allocating kv_cache 112MB
[03:18:42] request id=xyz seq_len=4096 model=redwood-34b:v3
[03:18:43] tail-latency 980ms p99 for tenant=stratus-corp
```

eng-luca: that kernel update might have changed allocator heuristics for kv cache. Two options: 1) roll back kernel on pool, 2) immediately change tenant routing to a smaller safe variant.

sre_jordan: prefer option 2 for immediate mitigation — less blast radius and faster to enact. We should pin the tenant to a safe variant and enable fallback to a smaller model. Plan: set tenant routing override -> model=redwood-7b-quant-safe, enable canary 10% to test then 100% if metrics improve. Also keep dedicated capacity but prevent new allocations of large kv_cache per request.

nira: command to pin (ops):
```
redwood routing override set --tenant stratus-corp --pool stratus-prod-pool --model redwood-7b-quant-safe --force
redwood routing override policy add --tenant stratus-corp --on-metric latency>250ms --fallback redwood-7b-compat
```

maya_oncall: executing now. Applying canary 10% -> 03:22:10Z

incident-bot: action recorded: routing override set by maya_oncall at 1812345730. Canary started at 10%.

ellen_csm: customer update: telling them we’re routing a subset to a lower-memory variant to stabilize. They asked for a pinned configuration until we confirm kernel rollback is safe.

eng-luca: also adding a temporary quota to sequence length for that tenant to limit kv_cache growth:
```
redwood tenant update --tenant stratus-corp --max-seq 2048 --ttl 15m
```

sre_jordan: monitoring p99 and error rate. If canary p99 < 300ms and errors drop, we promote to 100% and leave override in place until kernel rollback tested in staging. If not, rollback kernel 20260315 on pool.

ops-bot: telemetry: canary metrics at 03:28Z -> p99 dropped from 980ms to 220ms for canary traffic, error rate down 95%.

nira: great. Promote to 100% when you’re ready. Also add audit tag and reason = "mitigation for OOM/latency".

maya_oncall: promoting to 100% now, adding audit tag. Command output: OK -> tenant stratus-corp now routed to redwood-7b-quant-safe (100%).

incident-bot: mitigation complete at 1812345795. Status: degraded -> contained. Next steps: run staging kernel rollback test, evaluate memory heuristics, and prepare a permanent routing policy for stratus-corp (pin to safe variant with optional burst to 34b under controlled conditions).

ellen_csm: I’ll draft a customer note: summary, what we changed, ETA for next update (kernel rollback test in 4 hours). Will include that we’ve pinned them to a safe variant to preserve availability.

eng-luca: I'll schedule the kernel rollback test on staging and run regression on kv cache. If it’s green we can roll out a tuned kernel with updated allocator flags rather than full rollback.

sre_jordan: handoff to next on-call @maya_oncall -> please keep monitoring for 4 hours and escalate if error rate >1% or p99 > 350ms.

maya_oncall: ack, monitoring dashboards up. I’ll post updates in this thread.

incident-bot: incident P2 -> contained. Filed follow-up ticket: INF-5921 (kernel-heuristics + tenant-safe-routing).
